\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিগড়ানো} (bigṛāno)}{বিগড়ানো (bigṛāno)}]{\bn{বিগড়ানো} (bigṛāno) — to break down; to go wrong}

\label{lesson:BN-C394-bigrano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to run out, then the Bengali for to start (an engine).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিগড়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{বিগড়ানো}} — \emph{bigṛāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to break down; to go wrong\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পথে} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{গাড়িটা} \bn{বিগড়ে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pôthe āmāder gāṛiṭā bigṛe gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our car broke down on the way.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{গাড়ি} \bn{বিগড়ে} \bn{গেল}, \emph{sei gāṛi bigṛe gelô}.

Mostly in the -\bn{এ} form with \bn{যাওয়া}: \bn{বিগড়ে} \bn{যাওয়া}, of a machine, and of a mood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিগড়ানো}} (\emph{bigṛāno}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{bigṛā}, \textquotedblleft{}to go bad\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vighaṭatē}, \textquotedblleft{}flies apart, is marred\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11673); the machine sense is the modern use.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bigṛāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bigṛāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôthe āmāder gāṛiṭā bigṛe gelô.} — Our car broke down on the way.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to run out, then the Bengali for to start (an engine), then say \emph{bigṛāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বিগড়ানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To break down; to go wrong\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{যন্ত্রাংশ} (jôntrāngshô)}{যন্ত্রাংশ (jôntrāngshô)}]{\bn{যন্ত্রাংশ} (jôntrāngshô) — a spare part; a part of a machine}

\label{lesson:BN-C394-jontrangsho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to start (an engine), then the Bengali for to break down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{যন্ত্রাংশ}}
\textbf{\bn{যন্ত্রাংশ}} — \emph{jôntrāngshô} — \textquotedblleft{}a spare part; a part of a machine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{মিস্ত্রি} \bn{দোকান} \bn{থেকে} \bn{নতুন} \bn{যন্ত্রাংশ} \bn{আনলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mistri dokān theke nôtun jôntrāngshô ānlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mechanic brought a new part from the shop.
\end{quote}

A careful word, common on bills and in shops that sell them.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{যন্ত্রাংশ}} (\emph{jôntrāngshô}) joins Sanskrit \emph{yantra}, \textquotedblleft{}an instrument, a machine\textquotedblright{}, to \emph{aṃśa}, \textquotedblleft{}a part, a share\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams for both): a part of a machine; \bn{যন্ত্র} on its own is already taught.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôntrāngshô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôntrāngshô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mistri dokān theke nôtun jôntrāngshô ānlen.} — The mechanic brought a new part from the shop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to start (an engine), then the Bengali for to break down, then say \emph{jôntrāngshô} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্ক্রু} (skru)}{স্ক্রু (skru)}]{\bn{স্ক্রু} (skru) — a screw}

\label{lesson:BN-C394-skru}

Before the new one: say the Bengali for to break down, then the Bengali for a spare part.

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্টিয়ারিং} (sṭiyāring)}{স্টিয়ারিং (sṭiyāring)}]{\bn{স্টিয়ারিং} (sṭiyāring) — a steering wheel}

\label{lesson:BN-C394-stiyaring}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a spare part, then the Bengali for a screw.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{স্টিয়ারিং}}
\textbf{\bn{স্টিয়ারিং}} — \emph{sṭiyāring} — \textquotedblleft{}a steering wheel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\textbf{\bn{স্টিয়ারিং}} (\emph{sṭiyāring}) is borrowed from English \emph{steering}, short for \emph{steering wheel}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঘষা} (ghôshā)}{ঘষা (ghôshā)}]{\bn{ঘষা} (ghôshā) — to rub; to scrub}

\label{lesson:BN-C394-ghosha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a screw, then the Bengali for a steering wheel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঘষা}}
\textbf{\bn{ঘষা}} — \emph{ghôshā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rub; to scrub\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অরুণ} \bn{সাবান} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{সাইকেলের} \bn{চাকা} \bn{ঘষল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôrun sābān niye sāikeler chākā ghôshlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Arun took some soap and scrubbed the bicycle wheel.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{চাকাটা} \bn{ঘষলেন}, \emph{tini chākāṭā ghôshlen}.

The second letter is \bn{ষ}, said sh like \bn{শ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঘষা}} (\emph{ghôshā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{ghasā}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ghárṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}rubs\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4450).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
